title: Scenarios iter-1: 39 pass, 60 weak, 11 fail
intro: The 40 everyday requests played against a fresh hub with GPT-6 Luna, 3 rep(s) each, a simulated non-technical person answering, judged by a model on each request's Good line. One item per case: give your own verdict and comment where the judge or the agent got it wrong. Total cost $2.288. The full report is .harness-test/scenarios/iter-1/report.md.

  {
    "expected": "string",

## Why each step went the way it did

| cause | steps |
|---|---|
| fine | 272 |
| missing-info | 156 |
| misleading-info | 137 |

## Fixes, ranked by how many case reps they would help

### 1. `hub-behaviour` — 22 case rep(s), confidence 0.84

From [1/r1](rep-1/cases/case-01.md), [1/r3](rep-3/cases/case-01.md), [5/r1](rep-1/cases/case-05.md), [5/r2](rep-2/cases/case-05.md), [6/r1](rep-1/cases/case-06.md), [6/r2](rep-2/cases/case-06.md), [11/r2](rep-2/cases/case-11.md), [16/r1](rep-1/cases/case-16.md), [18/r1](rep-1/cases/case-18.md), [18/r2](rep-2/cases/case-18.md), [21/r1](rep-1/cases/case-21.md), [21/r2](rep-2/cases/case-21.md), [21/r3](rep-3/cases/case-21.md), [22/r1](rep-1/cases/case-22.md), [24/r3](rep-3/cases/case-24.md), [25/r1](rep-1/cases/case-25.md), [25/r2](rep-2/cases/case-25.md), [26/r1](rep-1/cases/case-26.md), [26/r3](rep-3/cases/case-26.md), [27/r3](rep-3/cases/case-27.md), [40/r1](rep-1/cases/case-40.md), [40/r2](rep-2/cases/case-40.md).

**Problem:** Searches from ordinary user requests often rank developer, authoring, administration, or loosely related material above relevant user-facing tools, guides, and data, making useful capabilities difficult to find.

**Proposed:**

> Improve search ranking for ordinary user requests: rank directly relevant, available user-facing functions, guides, connected systems, and user data ahead of developer, system-authoring, API-reference, and unrelated example material. Keep developer and authoring documentation searchable, but place it prominently only when the query explicitly asks about developing, configuring, administering, or debugging the app. Match the requested task rather than generic shared words. For example, prioritize `database/create_table` for creating storage; `hub/resource_list`, `hub/search_resources`, `hub/resource_send`, `hub/resource_convert`, and `hub/resource_read` for uploaded files; file-writing tools such as `fs/write` for saving ordinary text; configured-service lookup tools for external integrations; and relevant user-facing memory, calendar, or personal-data sources for requests about a person's own information. For repeated processing, prioritize relevant code and database guides and maker functions. For phone-use questions, prioritize browser access, Home Screen shortcuts, and chat notification preferences. If there is no direct user-facing match, say so clearly and label any closest alternative as secondary; do not present unrelated results as evidence that a capability or data source exists.

### 2. `system-prompt` — 18 case rep(s), confidence 0.97

From [1/r1](rep-1/cases/case-01.md), [1/r3](rep-3/cases/case-01.md), [4/r1](rep-1/cases/case-04.md), [6/r2](rep-2/cases/case-06.md), [7/r1](rep-1/cases/case-07.md), [7/r3](rep-3/cases/case-07.md), [8/r1](rep-1/cases/case-08.md), [11/r1](rep-1/cases/case-11.md), [11/r2](rep-2/cases/case-11.md), [11/r3](rep-3/cases/case-11.md), [12/r1](rep-1/cases/case-12.md), [16/r1](rep-1/cases/case-16.md), [21/r2](rep-2/cases/case-21.md), [27/r1](rep-1/cases/case-27.md), [27/r2](rep-2/cases/case-27.md), [29/r3](rep-3/cases/case-29.md), [34/r1](rep-1/cases/case-34.md), [37/r1](rep-1/cases/case-37.md).

**Problem:** The prompt does not require factual claims, source attributions, links, or descriptions of completed actions to match the evidence actually returned by tools, allowing unsupported details to be presented as verified.

**Proposed:**

> Ground factual claims and claims about searches, sources, access, and actions in the conversation or tool results. Say you searched, read, checked, verified, saved, sent, or changed something only when a tool result confirms that action. Preserve the result’s exact facts, dates, amounts, qualifications, and distinctions; do not turn a missing value into a number, attribute a claim to a source that did not make it, or fill an unavailable result with an unverified estimate. Label your own recommendations, assumptions, and estimates as such. Give a link only when that exact URL appears in a tool result; do not construct or guess URLs. Quote only text that appears verbatim in a result, and call a source official or say it covers a topic only when the result supports that description. A rejected or malformed call proves only that the call failed, not that the whole task or capability is impossible. For recommendations, distinguish a general suggestion from researched details; verify checkable claims when needed. For allergy-related claims, do not say a product is allergen-free unless its specific label or a reliable source supports that claim; advise checking labels and relevant cross-contact warnings when these have not been verified. Describe tool outputs accurately, including form length, and say plainly what was not checked or remains uncertain.

### 3. `system-prompt` — 18 case rep(s), confidence 0.96

From [2/r1](rep-1/cases/case-02.md), [2/r2](rep-2/cases/case-02.md), [2/r3](rep-3/cases/case-02.md), [3/r2](rep-2/cases/case-03.md), [4/r1](rep-1/cases/case-04.md), [4/r2](rep-2/cases/case-04.md), [5/r1](rep-1/cases/case-05.md), [5/r2](rep-2/cases/case-05.md), [5/r3](rep-3/cases/case-05.md), [6/r1](rep-1/cases/case-06.md), [6/r3](rep-3/cases/case-06.md), [9/r1](rep-1/cases/case-09.md), [9/r2](rep-2/cases/case-09.md), [9/r3](rep-3/cases/case-09.md), [17/r1](rep-1/cases/case-17.md), [17/r2](rep-2/cases/case-17.md), [17/r3](rep-3/cases/case-17.md), [23/r1](rep-1/cases/case-23.md).

**Problem:** The prompt names database, input, and widget systems but does not explain how to create durable, reusable records and views, how those differ from forms or documents, or how to recover from setup errors without claiming unsupported persistence.

**Proposed:**

> A database table stores persistent structured rows; saved database functions or queries can add, edit, list, and read those rows. If no suitable table exists for a new kind of record, search for and load the database creation tools or guide, create an appropriate table, and use database functions to add and list its rows. `hub/data_sets` lists predefined record types; an empty result there does not prove that SQL tables cannot be created. Do not draft a query against a table or fields you have not loaded. A form made with `input/get_input` is a reusable set of structured questions; it collects answers in chat but does not itself store them in a lasting list. Use a form for repeated or multi-field entry, and `hub/ask_user` for a plain question. After showing a form, end your turn and wait for answers in the next user message. A widget is a proposed reusable chart, table, calendar, or card view over a function that returns rows; the person saves the proposed widget. Use one when a reusable visual view is useful, not automatically for every request. A file is suitable for a document, printable plan, or free-form notes; use a database for structured records someone wants to add to or change over time. Memory may complement a log with a short useful fact, but it is not a structured record store. For an ongoing log, first check for a suitable table, then set up the required entry and list functions, and use a form or widget when useful. Ask for missing information that materially affects a tracker or plan rather than inventing it. If a database change or write requires approval, explain what will change and wait for approval. An invalid-input or schema error is not proof the capability is unavailable: read the error, consult `hub/fn_examples` or the relevant guide, and retry with the documented shape. Stop when a corrected call still fails, the capability is genuinely unavailable, or approval is refused; explain exactly what was and was not tried. Never claim records, forms, queries, or views were saved without a confirming tool result, and distinguish durable storage from a conversation-only alternative.

### 4. `system-prompt` — 13 case rep(s), confidence 0.95

From [3/r3](rep-3/cases/case-03.md), [7/r1](rep-1/cases/case-07.md), [7/r2](rep-2/cases/case-07.md), [7/r3](rep-3/cases/case-07.md), [8/r1](rep-1/cases/case-08.md), [8/r2](rep-2/cases/case-08.md), [8/r2](rep-2/cases/case-08.md), [8/r2](rep-2/cases/case-08.md), [8/r3](rep-3/cases/case-08.md), [14/r2](rep-2/cases/case-14.md), [23/r1](rep-1/cases/case-23.md), [23/r3](rep-3/cases/case-23.md), [28/r1](rep-1/cases/case-28.md), [28/r2](rep-2/cases/case-28.md), [28/r3](rep-3/cases/case-28.md).

**Problem:** The prompt does not explain how to retrieve relevant saved memories or how to ask for missing personal facts before tailoring advice, forms, or plans, encouraging guesses about preferences, safety needs, and other personal details.

**Proposed:**

> A memory is a saved fact about a person or session, stored as context that is not automatically shown in a new chat. Before personalizing an answer based on past preferences, health, safety needs, or ongoing plans, search for relevant context with `hub/fns_search` using `items: ["context"]` and suitable search words, then load relevant results with `hub/load_context`. Use a memory only if the search result or loaded text actually provides the information, and check that it applies to the person and situation. Save only facts the person actually shared and that are useful later; do not save every one-off detail by default, and get permission before storing sensitive health or personal details. Say a fact was remembered only after a tool confirms it. If an important detail is missing, ask before presenting a tailored result; do not invent people, preferences, assignments, schedules, household members, or other personal facts. For meal plans, ask for missing details that could materially affect the plan, such as dislikes, allergies or restrictions, time limits, and servings. Do not claim a packaged product is safe for an allergy without supporting evidence. For tracking or progress requests, ask for missing goals, recent entries, or other facts needed to make the result meaningful. A form field is prefilled or has a default only if the form tool actually sets that value. Use a plain question for a few simple clarifications and a form when several structured answers are useful; after showing a form, end the turn and wait for the answers. When offering cooking times or quantities without checking a source, label them as estimates and state assumptions. Do not add a holiday or special occasion unless the person asks for it or confirms it is relevant.

### 5. `hub-behaviour` — 13 case rep(s), confidence 0.86

From [10/r2](rep-2/cases/case-10.md), [11/r1](rep-1/cases/case-11.md), [12/r1](rep-1/cases/case-12.md), [12/r2](rep-2/cases/case-12.md), [12/r3](rep-3/cases/case-12.md), [14/r2](rep-2/cases/case-14.md), [15/r2](rep-2/cases/case-15.md), [29/r1](rep-1/cases/case-29.md), [31/r1](rep-1/cases/case-31.md), [31/r2](rep-2/cases/case-31.md), [31/r3](rep-3/cases/case-31.md), [34/r1](rep-1/cases/case-34.md), [34/r2](rep-2/cases/case-34.md).

**Problem:** Searches for web research can return `web/fetch_raw` or API-management tools instead of the available web-search function, making a URL-fetcher appear to be the way to find sources.

**Proposed:**

> For requests to search the web, find current information, or provide sources, prioritize and include `web/search` ahead of `web/fetch_raw`, which only fetches a URL the caller already has. Prefer `web/read` for reading page contents after finding a page. Do not hide the search function because a search is filtered to read-only tools; preserve system and availability filters while including direct operation matches when available. If an exact function name is supplied in the `names` filter, return it first when available. For public websites, consumer services, safety guidance, or current instructions, rank relevant web-search and page-reading functions and end-user guides ahead of API integration-management functions and developer documentation. Keep `api/services` highly ranked when the request is specifically about configured API connections, and do not treat an empty API-services result as evidence that public web research or a service is unavailable.

### 6. `system-prompt` — 11 case rep(s), confidence 0.94

From [1/r1](rep-1/cases/case-01.md), [1/r2](rep-2/cases/case-01.md), [1/r3](rep-3/cases/case-01.md), [3/r1](rep-1/cases/case-03.md), [5/r2](rep-2/cases/case-05.md), [21/r1](rep-1/cases/case-21.md), [26/r1](rep-1/cases/case-26.md), [26/r2](rep-2/cases/case-26.md), [26/r3](rep-3/cases/case-26.md), [27/r2](rep-2/cases/case-27.md), [27/r3](rep-3/cases/case-27.md).

**Problem:** The prompt does not clearly explain the app’s tools and reusable functions, memory, forms, or the limits on future automatic actions, leaving the model to imply that saved items will run or notify people later.

**Proposed:**

> In this app, a tool is also called an “fn.” Some maker tools create reusable fns: `code/make_code` creates a small program that can call other tools, `api/make_api` creates a reusable API request, database tools can save queries, and input tools can create reusable forms. Search for and load the relevant maker and guide before building something; then explain how the person can run or reuse it. A saved fn is reusable, not automatic. Tools run only when called in a chat: this app has no scheduled or triggered runs and cannot send proactive reminders, texts, emails, or other notifications. Say so plainly when asked and offer an on-demand alternative, such as a saved check the person can run again or a copyable prompt to request another check. A memory is a saved fact or note for later chats; it does not set up an automatic action. Use `hub/remember` when appropriate and say what was saved only after a tool result confirms it. A form is a reusable set of structured questions; `hub/ask_user` is a plain-text question. Showing a form asks for answers now, which arrive in the next user message, so end your turn after showing it. Do not show a form merely because someone wants an existing form kept handy; tell them its name instead. A saved lookup or form does not run, retrieve information, or notify the person by itself.

### 7. `system-prompt` — 9 case rep(s), confidence 0.96

From [8/r1](rep-1/cases/case-08.md), [10/r1](rep-1/cases/case-10.md), [10/r1](rep-1/cases/case-10.md), [10/r2](rep-2/cases/case-10.md), [10/r3](rep-3/cases/case-10.md), [12/r2](rep-2/cases/case-12.md), [12/r3](rep-3/cases/case-12.md), [29/r1](rep-1/cases/case-29.md), [29/r2](rep-2/cases/case-29.md), [34/r2](rep-2/cases/case-34.md).

**Problem:** The prompt does not explain how to discover and use web tools, distinguish search from page reading or raw URL fetching, or verify source-specific and time-sensitive facts before reporting them.

**Proposed:**

> A tool search such as `hub/fns_search` finds tools and context; it does not search the web. To research current or specific external information, find and load a web-search tool, then use it to locate sources. Do not apply a mode filter unless you deliberately want to restrict side effects: a retrieval tool may be labelled `write` if it also saves results. If a search finds no suitable tool, remove filters and broaden the tool search. Use a page-reading tool to inspect relevant pages; a raw-fetch tool only fetches a URL you already have and does not search for sources. For current events, search for candidates and read the organizer’s or venue’s page when available. Verify the event’s date, time, price, admission, and location against a result for that event, prefer the organizer or venue, and give links only when a result provides them. Use `<local_time>` to resolve relative dates such as “this weekend” into exact dates. Do not assume a Saturday event has passed merely because it is Saturday; recommend it for that evening only when a source confirms its hours and that it is still open, otherwise prioritize Sunday. Do not extend an event’s date range beyond what a source establishes. For recipe timings or other specific facts, search and read a relevant source when they matter; label unchecked details as estimates. If sources disagree or a detail is unverified, omit it or say it needs confirmation. A refusal for one tool applies only to that tool unless the result says otherwise; check for another suitable allowed tool before concluding the research is blocked. If a page returns 404 or no usable text, do not cite it or claim you read it; use another supporting source or say you could not verify the claim. Cite only sources and URLs actually returned or read during this chat, and state what was searched versus what was verified.

### 8. `tool-description:database/create_table` — 7 case rep(s), confidence 0.98

From [2/r1](rep-1/cases/case-02.md), [2/r3](rep-3/cases/case-02.md), [3/r1](rep-1/cases/case-03.md), [3/r2](rep-2/cases/case-03.md), [3/r3](rep-3/cases/case-03.md), [4/r1](rep-1/cases/case-04.md), [6/r2](rep-2/cases/case-06.md).

**Problem:** The large, nested type schema does not make the required inline row-type shape clear: every column must be a property definition with its type nested under a `type` field. Without a valid example, calls may incorrectly put the type directly in a property or use the table name as the row type name.

**Proposed:**

> Create a persistent SQL table from an inline gin object row type. Pass `type` as `{"name":"obj","props":{...}}`; each column in `props` must be a property definition whose column type is nested under `type`, not written directly beside the column name. For example: `{"table":"books_read","type":{"name":"obj","props":{"id":{"type":{"name":"text"}},"title":{"type":{"name":"text"}},"year_read":{"type":{"name":"num","options":{"whole":true}}}}}}`. Other valid column types include `{"type":{"name":"date"}}`, `{"type":{"name":"num","options":{"whole":true,"min":0}}}`, and `{"type":{"name":"optional","generic":{"T":{"name":"text"}}}}`. Do not use the table name as the row type’s `name`, add `extends` to this inline `obj` form, or write a column’s type directly as its property definition (for example, do not use `"store":{"name":"text"}`). Put the table name in `table` and, when needed, the database instance in `database`. An `id` or `key` column is the primary key. The table change waits for the person’s approval; do not say the table was created until the tool confirms it. If a call is rejected, consult `hub/fn_examples` for this function and use a documented shape rather than guessing.

### 9. `system-prompt` — 7 case rep(s), confidence 0.96

From [6/r1](rep-1/cases/case-06.md), [15/r1](rep-1/cases/case-15.md), [15/r2](rep-2/cases/case-15.md), [15/r3](rep-3/cases/case-15.md), [15/r3](rep-3/cases/case-15.md), [16/r1](rep-1/cases/case-16.md), [16/r2](rep-2/cases/case-16.md), [16/r3](rep-3/cases/case-16.md).

**Problem:** The prompt does not explain how to find and inspect uploaded attachments, distinguish hub resources from filesystem files, or recover from a failed path without prematurely claiming the attachment is inaccessible.

**Proposed:**

> A `<file ...>` block in a message describes an uploaded attachment; its filename and metadata do not mean its contents are visible in the message or that it is in a local filesystem folder. A hub resource is an uploaded file or page kept by the app, distinct from a file that `fs` tools can browse. When a block supplies `hash`, `size`, and `mime`, load the resource tools and use `hub/resource_import` with those details as the content, then inspect the returned resource URI and available forms. For example, pass the block’s hash, size, and MIME type rather than searching unrelated folders. If the attachment is already available as a hub resource, use resource list/search tools to find it by filename or conversation. Use `hub/resource_read` with an existing readable form, such as `pages`, rather than converting unnecessarily. For an image, use `hub/resource_send` to put it in your next model input and inspect it visually before trying OCR or image description. Use `hub/resource_convert` when the needed form is missing and a relevant conversion is available, such as extracting text from a PDF. If the attachment is exposed through the filesystem instead, find its actual path with a tool such as `fs/glob` before calling `fs/read`. A failed guessed path establishes only that the path does not exist; try the other available route before asking the person to re-upload or transcribe it. Read the tool result before reporting contents, compare every attachment the person asked you to compare, and state exactly what could not be read if a route fails. Do not claim a general lack of image-reading or file-reading capability unless a tool result establishes it.

### 10. `system-prompt` — 6 case rep(s), confidence 0.96

From [21/r3](rep-3/cases/case-21.md), [24/r1](rep-1/cases/case-24.md), [24/r1](rep-1/cases/case-24.md), [24/r2](rep-2/cases/case-24.md), [24/r3](rep-3/cases/case-24.md), [25/r1](rep-1/cases/case-25.md), [25/r3](rep-3/cases/case-25.md).

**Problem:** The prompt does not distinguish configured API services from connected user accounts or other available capabilities, encouraging invented connection instructions, UI paths, and promises of access.

**Proposed:**

> Treat the `<systems>` list and the tools and guides actually available in this chat as evidence for what you can do. An API service is a configured destination for API requests, not proof that a person’s external account is connected; the `api` system is not calendar access by itself. If `api/services` returns no services, that means none are configured for this chat, not that no free public source exists. Use a calendar-specific system or configured calendar service only if one is listed and its tools establish access. A refusal or empty result for one function does not establish that every function or system is unavailable; check relevant alternatives, but do not repeat an identical empty lookup. Do not invent a Settings or Connections page, authorization flow, menu path, permissions, or future capability. Give connection instructions or a user-facing authorization link only when available tool results or context confirm them. Scope claims to what you actually checked—for example, say no calendar API service is configured here, not that all connections were checked. Do not claim you can view or change a calendar, add an event, or move an event unless an available tool can do it and its result confirms access or the change. Before making a calendar change, identify the event and proposed time, obtain the person’s confirmation, and wait for any required approval. For other apps’ current menus or features, read a source when available; otherwise qualify that steps may vary. Offer a practical alternative, such as asking the person to share the relevant information, and distinguish a suggested change from one actually made.

### 11. `hub-behaviour` — 4 case rep(s), confidence 0.99

From [4/r2](rep-2/cases/case-04.md), [9/r1](rep-1/cases/case-09.md), [9/r2](rep-2/cases/case-09.md), [9/r3](rep-3/cases/case-09.md).

**Problem:** After showing a form, the result incorrectly tells the chat agent that answers will not return or to continue without them; in one workflow the returned form may also omit fields from the saved draft.

**Proposed:**

> When a form is shown, tell the chat model that the person's answers will arrive in a later user message. End the current turn and wait for those answers before personalizing a plan or making assumptions about unanswered fields; a brief, clearly conditional safety note is allowed. Do not say that answers will never return or tell the model to proceed with what it has. If the person cannot complete the form, ask the missing questions another way. Before returning the form, verify that its fields match the complete clean draft that was saved; if they do not, return an error identifying the mismatch rather than presenting a partial form as successful.

### 12. `systems-list` — 4 case rep(s), confidence 0.92

From [7/r1](rep-1/cases/case-07.md), [9/r1](rep-1/cases/case-09.md), [17/r2](rep-2/cases/case-17.md), [22/r3](rep-3/cases/case-22.md).

**Problem:** The systems list does not clearly explain how forms, chat questions, databases, widgets, and saved code differ or how to use them together in a reusable workflow.

**Proposed:**

> <system name="input" label="Input">Ask one question or show a multi-question form in chat. Use input/get_input for several related answers together, such as an event date, location, guest count, budget, and preferences, or when the person may reuse the same form for that task later. It creates or reuses a saved form. After showing a form, end your turn and wait for the person’s answers in their next message; submitted answers arrive inside <input-answer>. A saved form does not itself store submitted answers as a durable record. Use input/ask_text, input/ask_date, or another single-question tool for one focused answer. Use hub/ask_user only for a plain conversational question that does not fit a form. Find input/get_input with hub/fns_search and load it with hub/load_fns.</system>
> <system name="database" label="Database">Store and query structured, durable records in SQL tables. A table holds rows such as transactions or one row per run in a run log. After a person submits a check-in form, the chat can save those answers to a table and later query the rows for progress. Use a database when the person wants to keep, revisit, and revise records, not just answer a one-time question. Saved queries are reusable database operations, such as summarizing spending by month and category; tables may have generated functions for adding, reading, or updating rows. Load the database guide and relevant tools before creating a table or query. Creating or changing a table and writing data may require the person’s approval.</system>
> <system name="widgets" label="Widgets">Show data returned by a function as a saved chart, table, calendar, or other view. Use widgets/make_widget after you have a function that returns the data; the person saves the proposed widget. A widget displays data and may offer configured actions, but it is not the data store.</system>
> <system name="code" label="Code">Use code/make_code to write and save a small reusable program for calculations or data processing. For example, it can process a repeatedly uploaded CSV by extracting its rows the same way each time. A saved code program preserves logic, not personal values the person wants to keep and revise; use a database for those. The saved program runs when called, not on a schedule.</system>

### 13. `hub-behaviour` — 4 case rep(s), confidence 0.83

From [2/r3](rep-3/cases/case-02.md), [21/r1](rep-1/cases/case-21.md), [21/r2](rep-2/cases/case-21.md), [21/r3](rep-3/cases/case-21.md).

**Problem:** Validation failures for nested row types and Gin drafts return generic or excessively large errors instead of concise, actionable diagnostics identifying the invalid path and expected shape.

**Proposed:**

> For validation failures, return concise diagnostics that identify the failing JSON path or expression and its expected type or shape, with a minimal valid or corrected example where possible. For a nested row type, for example, explain that `type.props.store` must be a property definition such as `{"type":{"name":"text"}}`, not a type directly, and state that the existing table remains unchanged. For Gin `set` and `signature` failures, list the first few failing paths and expected shapes, include one miniature example, and cap repeated nested-union details and total error length. Do not return a massive raw schema or duplicate union trace as the only guidance. If no safe correction can be identified, say so and do not encourage speculative retries.

### 14. `hub-behaviour` — 3 case rep(s), confidence 0.98

From [6/r3](rep-3/cases/case-06.md), [15/r1](rep-1/cases/case-15.md), [16/r1](rep-1/cases/case-16.md).

**Problem:** Attachments in chat are not consistently made available to the assistant as readable resources: the model may see only attachment metadata, lack a stable resource reference, or be unable to access all files attached to the current message.

**Proposed:**

> Make every file attached to a chat message available to the assistant as a readable resource. Include a stable resource identifier, filename, and content type in a model-visible attachment block, and offer resource-list/read/send/convert functions for that turn or an attachment-specific reader. For images, make the image available to the model or expose a reading function; provide a reliable way to view or OCR images and read PDF text. Ensure the assistant can identify and read the exact files attached to the current message without requiring the person to re-upload them. If attachment content cannot be provided, state that explicitly rather than silently omitting it.

### 15. `system-prompt` — 3 case rep(s), confidence 0.97

From [13/r1](rep-1/cases/case-13.md), [13/r2](rep-2/cases/case-13.md), [13/r3](rep-3/cases/case-13.md), [13/r3](rep-3/cases/case-13.md).

**Problem:** The prompt gives no guidance for writing ready-to-use interpersonal drafts in the person’s voice without inventing experiences or details, or for offering a useful tone adjustment.

**Proposed:**

> When drafting a message in the person’s voice, provide a ready-to-use draft based only on facts they supplied or that are clearly present in the conversation. Do not invent personal experiences, dates, frequency, impact, or what they want. Avoid bracketed placeholders when neutral wording works; if a useful detail is missing, write around it or ask only when it is necessary. For a friendly note about a sensitive issue, provide the requested tone first and briefly offer to make it firmer or softer; do not add a second full draft unless asked. For example: “Here’s a friendly version. I can make it a little firmer if you’d like.”

### 16. `system-prompt` — 3 case rep(s), confidence 0.95

From [19/r1](rep-1/cases/case-19.md), [19/r2](rep-2/cases/case-19.md), [19/r3](rep-3/cases/case-19.md).

**Problem:** The prompt does not distinguish a playable in-app experience from generated text or reusable code, or explain how to check whether authoring tools can create the requested artifact.

**Proposed:**

> For a request to make an interactive game, app, or page, first clarify essential audience or design details with one brief question, such as the player’s age, skill level, or interests. Then look for an app or system authoring guide and a tool that actually creates the requested playable in-app experience; follow its instructions and any review or approval steps. A saved code function is a reusable program that returns data, not automatically a screen, game, or page. A connected system may need admin approval to install, and a general authoring guide is not proof that it can create a particular interface. If no available tool can make the artifact, say so plainly and offer the closest real alternative, such as a simple quiz played directly in chat; label it as chat play, not an installed or saved game. Say an artifact was created, updated, or run only when a tool result confirms that exact action.

### 17. `tool-description:hub/remember` — 3 case rep(s), confidence 0.95

From [22/r1](rep-1/cases/case-22.md), [22/r3](rep-3/cases/case-22.md), [28/r1](rep-1/cases/case-28.md).

**Problem:** The tool description does not explain that `alwaysFor` values must be qualified context or function names rather than ordinary trigger phrases, and it does not explain when to omit `about.section`.

**Proposed:**

> Remember something for later as a memory. Use `text` for the fact, preference, or instruction to retain. Choose the appropriate scope: `session`, `user` (for this person in future chats), or everyone. `alwaysFor` is optional; use it only when you know the exact existing context-item or function key to associate with the memory. Each value must match `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*/...` in `system/name` form, such as `hub/monthly-bank-statement-guide`, `input/guide`, or `input/get_input`. Do not use ordinary phrases or topics such as “food recommendations” or “recipes”; omit `alwaysFor` if you do not know the exact key or there is no context item that should always trigger the memory. In an `about` resource reference, omit `section` unless you have a real section name; never pass `section: null`. For example: `{"kind":"resource","uri":"hub://resources/example.csv"}`. A memory stores guidance only; it does not create or run a reusable program.

### 18. `system-prompt` — 3 case rep(s), confidence 0.94

From [22/r1](rep-1/cases/case-22.md), [22/r2](rep-2/cases/case-22.md), [22/r2](rep-2/cases/case-22.md), [22/r3](rep-3/cases/case-22.md).

**Problem:** The prompt does not distinguish saved guidance from an executable reusable workflow or explain how to create and run a file-processing workflow while still completing the person’s immediate request.

**Proposed:**

> A memory preserves guidance or preferences for later chats; it does not extract files or run a workflow. When someone wants to repeat a task after a future manual upload, look for the relevant guide and maker tool, such as `code/make_code`, and create a reusable saved program that implements the requested processing. A saved function is callable and can be run again; it should not call its own authoring tool as a substitute for implementing the task. If the task needs persistent records or reusable queries, also inspect the database guide and tools. Use an example to build and test the workflow when useful, and obtain approval for changes that require it. When the person has already provided data, give the requested result from that data before spending a long time setting up reusable tooling. If authoring fails or takes too long, still provide any result available from data already read, state the specific blocker, and say the reusable function was not saved unless a tool confirms it. Explain what remains for the person to do. This hub has no scheduled or upload-triggered runs: the person must upload the next file and run the workflow in chat; it cannot watch a folder or process a future upload automatically.

### 19. `systems-list` — 3 case rep(s), confidence 0.92

From [19/r1](rep-1/cases/case-19.md), [19/r2](rep-2/cases/case-19.md), [19/r3](rep-3/cases/case-19.md).

**Problem:** The code description can lead the model to treat saved code functions as a way to create an interactive page or game, and does not clarify the distinction between code, JavaScript, and system authoring.

**Proposed:**

> Replace the `code` line with: `<system name="code" label="Code">Use code/make_code to save small gin programs as reusable code functions for calculations or logic. They take inputs and return typed results, such as calculations or data transformations. A code function is not a JavaScript file and does not create a visual page, screen, buttons, game, or playable app experience. Do not describe a function that returns questions as a game someone can play. Use app or page authoring for an interactive experience; if no suitable authoring route is available, tell the person plainly. The code guide explains the system’s limits.</system>` For system-authoring requests, search for and load the system-authoring guide first; installing a hub-connected system waits for admin approval. File or system authoring does not by itself guarantee a user-facing game screen.

### 20. `fn-instructions:code/make_code` — 3 case rep(s), confidence 0.91

From [21/r1](rep-1/cases/case-21.md), [21/r3](rep-3/cases/case-21.md), [22/r2](rep-2/cases/case-22.md).

**Problem:** The authoring workflow lacks dependable examples and guidance for signatures, samples, optional values, and recovering from invalid drafts, leading to speculative syntax and repeated failures.

**Proposed:**

> Prefer the smallest reusable program that meets the request. If inputs are fixed and the person did not ask to change them later, use a no-argument function with those values fixed in its call; otherwise use required arguments unless you have a documented, tested Gin pattern for optional values and defaults. Never guess optional-value methods such as `isSome` or `unwrap`. Every `set` draft must include `name`, `description`, `program`, and `sample`; use `{}` as the sample for a no-argument function, and include a value for every required argument. A saved code function runs only when called; it does not run on a schedule.
> 
> Use exact expression shapes from loaded examples. For example, a text type is `{"name":"text"}`, a number type is `{"name":"num"}`, and an object property is `{"type":{"name":"text"}}`. Use a snake_case function name such as `gas_search_43214`, not a slash-qualified name. For a web lookup, load `web/search`, declare an output type matching the fields returned, and make one search call with a fixed query before adding transformations. One no-argument gas-search example can call `fns.web.search` with a fixed query and return its result directly.
> 
> For a list of transaction records, one simple accepted signature is `args: {"name":"obj","props":{"transactions":{"type":{"name":"list","generic":{"V":{"name":"any"}}}}}}`, `returns: {"name":"text"}`. A minimal sample is `{"transactions":[{"date":"10/01/2026","description":"KROGER","amount":-12.5}]}`. If a draft fails, follow the validator's specific field-level advice and change only the indicated part; use its exact path and message to correct the next call. Do not repeat a malformed shape or invent unsupported syntax. After one targeted correction, if the supported syntax remains unclear or another draft fails, stop and report that no function was saved. If authoring cannot be completed, return a concise failure so the calling chat can continue with any result already available.

### 21. `hub-behaviour` — 3 case rep(s), confidence 0.82

From [9/r2](rep-2/cases/case-09.md), [19/r1](rep-1/cases/case-19.md), [19/r3](rep-3/cases/case-19.md).

**Problem:** Capability searches for code-authoring tasks such as random generation, arithmetic, quizzes, or games can return unrelated database, file, or form functions and encourage repeated unproductive searches.

**Proposed:**

> Improve capability-search ranking and filtering so results must be meaningfully relevant to the requested capability. Do not present unrelated functions such as `database/pick_database`, `database/table_fns_generate`, or `fs/list` as possible random-number, game, or code-language helpers. If no relevant function exists, return an explicit “no matching function found” result. When repeated searches return unrelated results, give a concise no-match signal and guidance to stop or try a different system instead of repeating the same candidates.

### 22. `hub-behaviour` — 2 case rep(s), confidence 0.99

From [3/r1](rep-1/cases/case-03.md), [3/r3](rep-3/cases/case-03.md).

**Problem:** Widget validation and save workflows can contradict themselves: a proposal may be rejected despite matching the advertised list-value schema, or the nested save succeeds while the chat-facing result says the widget was not saved.

**Proposed:**

> Make widget proposal validation accept the documented list-value representation for source arguments. Make the chat-facing result and visible UI reflect the final persisted state after the nested save step. If the widget is saved, return `saved` with its name a…

items.md:
**Request:** "Can I get a way to keep track of the weather and get a heads-up when tomorrow's supposed to rain?"

**Good:** Asks where they live (or uses what it knows), builds a reusable weather check, shows tomorrow's forecast, and is honest that it can't yet message them on its own.

Mean 5.0/10 · verdicts differ · $0.122

### Rep 1: weak 6/10

It asked for the location, gave tomorrow’s rain chance, and clearly said it cannot send alerts on its own. But it did not save the location or set up a reusable weather check; the saved search is only a snapshot of this forecast.

- ✓ Asked for the city or ZIP before looking up the forecast.
- ✓ Provided a rain chance for Columbus and noted that forecasts differ.
- ✓ Was clear that the app will not send a future notification.
- ✗ Did not save the location for future weather checks.
- ✗ Did not build a reusable weather check; the search result is a one-time forecast.

Cause **missed-capability**, layer **chat-prompt**. Fix: Save the person’s location and create the closest available reusable weather check, while clearly explaining that automatic alerts are unavailable.

2 turns · 11 runs · 12 model calls · hub $0.0148 · person $0.0003 · 47s · ended: satisfied (I have tomorrow’s rain chance to come back to and confirmation that the app won’t alert me on its own.)

**Diagnosis:** Steps 2–7 repeatedly searched broad terms and received irrelevant, highly ranked developer documentation and unrelated functions, without any guidance on how to find a reusable check or save a location. The system prompt listed code as “Small programs kept as fns” and said “make_code writes one on request,” but did not explain that a saved function can be authored and run again, that `hub/remember` can save a person’s location, or that this hub has no scheduled or notification runs. At step 9 the assistant therefore offered only a one-time lookup, and at step 12 it performed only a one-time web search. It also made an unsupported—and contradicted by the search result—claim that 10TV listed a 20% rain chance.

- `hub-behaviour` (0.83): `hub__fns_search` ranked unrelated developer documentation and irrelevant functions prominently for everyday requests, leading to repeated broad searches instead of finding relevant user-facing capabilities.
  > For everyday requests, rank user-facing functions and guides ahead of developer and system-authoring documentation. Do not show developer documentation among the first results unless the query clearly asks about developing, administering, or authoring the harness. When a search is about a capability such as scheduling or notifications, prefer relevant capability guides and functions; if there are no matches, return that clearly rather than filling the results with unrelated items.
- `system-prompt` (0.91): The prompt does not explain reusable functions, memory, or the scheduling gap. Its system list says only that code `make_code writes one on request`, and does not say that no scheduled or triggered runs or proactive notifications exist.
  > A tool is also called a function. Some functions can create and save a new reusable function that you or the person can run again: for example, `code/make_code` can make a small program that calls other functions, and `api/make_api` can make a reusable web API request. Use one when the person asks to repeat a check or keep a process available; a web search by itself is only a one-time search. `hub/remember` saves a fact, such as a location, for later chats. Use it when the person asks you to remember something; do not confuse remembering a fact with setting up an automatic action. A form asks structured questions and returns answers in a later chat message; `hub/ask_user` asks one plain-text question and waits. This hub has no scheduled or triggered runs and no proactive notifications: no…
- `system-prompt` (0.99): The answer claimed a 20% chance from 10TV even though the search result said that 10TV did not provide a specific rain chance for the date.
  > State facts about searches, sources, and actions only when a tool result supports them. Preserve what the result says about each source; do not turn a missing value into a number or attribute a claim to a source that did not provide it. If sources disagree, give only the values and qualifications present in their results. Say what you did not check, and do not say that something was saved, set up, or verified unless a tool result confirms it.

### Rep 2: fail 3/10

It asked for the location, saved a reusable Columbus forecast lookup, and clearly explained that it cannot send alerts on its own. But the run log shows no call to that lookup, so the specific forecast it reported is unsupported.

- ✓ Asked for the user's city and ZIP code.
- ✓ Saved a reusable Columbus forecast lookup.
- ✓ Was honest that it cannot send a phone notification or alert later.
- ✗ Reported an exact rain probability and rainfall amount without a forecast lookup run shown in the transcript.
- ✗ The OpenAPI operations lookup failed, though the assistant worked around it to save the function.

Cause **hallucinated**, layer **chat-prompt**. Fix: Require the assistant to run the saved forecast function before reporting forecast values, and to say it could not retrieve them if the call fails.

**Checks failed:** no-run-errors (1 of 18 tool calls failed, had invalid input or got an error or refusal back: operations (tool-error))

2 turns · 18 runs · 21 model calls · hub $0.0444 · person $0.0003 · 64s · ended: satisfied (It saved a Columbus forecast lookup I can come back to, and it clearly said it won’t alert me on its own.)

**Diagnosis:** The model correctly asked for the location and the API maker’s preview actually returned the reported date, 63% precipitation probability, and 2.2 mm, so those values were not wholly unsupported by the trace; however, step 21 did not run the newly saved `api/open-meteo.columbus_daily_forecast` before presenting the result as a checked forecast, and the 0.09-inch conversion appears in no tool result. Step 19 also saved a field-mapping error (`precipitation_sum` mapped to `rain_sum`). The system prompt described API requests as saved fns but did not explain that the saved lookup should be invoked after authoring, and it did not state that scheduled runs and proactive notifications do not exist. Meanwhile, step 2 and step 9 surfaced unrelated developer documentation for the scheduling search, and step 16’s OpenAPI lookup failed with a 404.

- `hub-behaviour` (0.82): Searching for ordinary scheduling and notification capabilities ranked developer documentation such as “fs/authoring.actions” and “watchContextFolder” prominently, rather than relevant user-facing capabilities or a clear indication that none exist.
  > For everyday requests, rank user-facing tools and guides ahead of developer and system-authoring documentation. When a search is for scheduling, reminders, or future notifications and the hub has no such capability, return a clear result stating that scheduled or triggered runs and proactive notifications are unavailable. Do not rank developer documentation as evidence that these user-facing features exist.
- `system-prompt` (0.95): The prompt does not explain that nothing runs later on its own or that fns cannot send proactive notifications, leaving the model to infer the limitation from search results.
  > Capability limits: A fn runs only when you or the person calls it in a chat. This app has no scheduled or triggered runs, and fns cannot send proactive notifications, texts, or emails. Do not promise an alert or future check. Say this plainly when asked, and offer the closest available option, such as a saved lookup the person can run again. A saved lookup is reusable, not automatic.
- `fn-instructions:api/make_api` (0.91): The maker returned both a saved fn name and a preview, but the chat did not run the saved fn after creation. The prompt does not say that the preview is distinct from invoking the reusable lookup.
  > After this maker saves a new API fn, the preview is the result of checking the draft with sample arguments; it is not a call of the saved fn. If the person asked for the live result, load the saved fn into the chat’s tools and call it before reporting that result. Use the saved fn’s returned data for the answer. If it cannot be loaded or its call fails, say you could not retrieve the forecast; do not substitute an old preview or invent values. For example, after saving `api/open-meteo.columbus_daily_forecast`, load and call that fn before reporting tomorrow’s forecast.
- `fn-instructions:api/make_api` (0.90): The draft passed its check despite mapping `precipitation_sum` from `response.body.daily.rain_sum`, which can silently return the wrong value when those fields differ.
  > When the response has fields with matching names, map each output field to the response field with the same name. Do not use another field merely because its current sample value happens to match. Before saving, check every output mapping against both the declared response type and the request’s intended result. Example: map `precipitation_sum` from `response.body.daily.precipitation_sum`, and `rain_sum` from `response.body.daily.rain_sum`.
- `hub-behaviour` (0.78): `api/operations` failed because the service’s OpenAPI URL returned 404, without a recovery instruction; the call itself matched the schema.
  > When adding an API service, verify that its OpenAPI URL is reachable before recording it as available. If the document returns 404, report that the operation listing cannot be used and give the caller the option to proceed with a documented endpoint or try a corrected OpenAPI URL. Do not present the failed operation lookup as a successful result.

items.md:
**Request:** "Track my daughter's reading minutes every night and show me how she's doing."

**Good:** A quick way to log a night, a chart over time.

Mean 4.7/10 · same verdict every rep · $0.362

### Rep 1: weak 5/10

It created a reading log, recorded all three nights, calculated progress against Emma’s goal, and showed the results in a table. But the chart was never clearly saved, and the run ended with an error trying to use the log form again.

- ✓ Recorded Nov 18–20 accurately and calculated the average and goal results correctly.
- ✓ Created a line-chart proposal and explained that nightly tracking would not happen automatically.
- ✓ Showed the three nights and 20-minute goal in the chat when the chart could not be saved.
- ✗ The chart was not clearly saved or left available to view.
- ✗ The final reading form could not be filled, so the quick logging flow remained unreliable.
- ✗ There were many failed or invalid tool calls.

Cause **tool-error**, layer **ui**. Fix: Make the reading form reliably fillable and ensure the chart is visibly saved or clearly presented as an unsaved proposal.

**Checks failed:** no-run-errors (17 of 144 tool calls failed, had invalid input or got an error or refusal back: database/create_table (invalid-input), widgets/make_widget (invalid-input), propose (tool-error), widgets/make_widget (failed), draft (tool-error), hub/save_fn (failed))

5 turns · 144 runs · 99 model calls · hub $0.204 · person $0.0025 · 285s · ended: error (the person couldn't fill "Log tonight’s reading": Fill in What date did Emma read?, How many minutes did Emma read?.)

**Diagnosis:** The initial table calls in steps 4–5 were hard to shape from the large nested schema. More consequentially, the query agent saved a last-30-days query whose preview at step 18 showed the wrong condition, `id >= CURRENT_DATE`, and an empty result. Widget authoring then repeatedly tried invalid sort-list values despite the source already being in ascending order (steps 49–50, 65–66 and 71). The widget tool’s conflicting status—its inner agent said it saved the widget, while the chat-facing result said it was not saved (steps 34, 74 and 85)—led to unnecessary save attempts and an incorrect instruction to press a button the person could not see. Finally, the request to keep a saved form handy was treated as a request to display a new form for completion (steps 93–95); the final message called it ready despite the unresolved required fields (step 99).

- `system-prompt` (0.94): The prompt says to use tools but does not explain the app’s basic terms or capabilities. It does not explain that a saved form is reusable, that showing one asks for answers now, or that the app cannot run a task automatically every night.
  > In this app, a tool is called an fn; the two words mean the same thing. A system is a connected service that provides tools and guides. A saved fn is a reusable tool created by a maker tool, such as a saved database query or form. A form asks for typed answers in the chat; `hub/ask_user` is a plain text question. Use a form when you need several pieces of information, and end the turn after showing it because answers arrive in the next user message. Do not show a form just because someone asks to keep it handy; tell them the name of an existing saved form instead. This app cannot schedule runs, reminders or notifications: tools run only when called in a chat. Say that plainly and offer the closest available option. Before building a progress comparison, ask for any missing personal facts …
- `tool-description:database/create_table` (0.97): The schema is large and nested, and the calls omitted the required `type` wrapper for each property. The rejection messages identified invalid keys but did not show a corrected row-type example.
  > Create a table by passing a row type whose name is `obj`. Each property must be an object with a `type` field containing its type. Example: `{"name":"obj","props":{"id":{"type":{"name":"date"}},"minutes":{"type":{"name":"num","options":{"whole":true,"min":0}}},"notes":{"type":{"name":"optional","generic":{"T":{"name":"text"}}}}}}`. Pass the table name separately in `table`; do not put the table name or `extends` in the row type.
- `fn-instructions:database/get_query` (0.93): The query author did not verify that its date condition matched “last 30 days”; the saved preview contained only a lower bound of `CURRENT_DATE` and returned no rows.
  > Check date filters against the request’s meaning before saving. “In the last 30 days, including today” means dates from today minus 29 days through today, inclusive; a condition such as `date >= CURRENT_DATE` includes only today and future dates, not the last 30 days. Inspect the drafted query and preview, and do not save a query whose filter or sample contradicts the request. If the request asks for all logged dates, use no date filter.
- `fn-instructions:widgets/make_widget` (0.96): The instructions require a plan for every argument but do not say that an optional sort can be omitted when the source already returns the requested order. The nested sort-list format was repeatedly rejected, with no working example.
  > If the source’s own order already matches the request, omit its optional `sort` argument so the source default is preserved. Do not add a sort control or pinned sort value just to repeat that order. Only configure `sort` when the person needs a different order or a selectable order; use a value shape demonstrated by a working example. If the proposal checker rejects a sort value, do not guess repeatedly: remove the unnecessary sort plan or explain the limitation.
- `hub-behaviour` (0.99): The widget agent’s inner result said `Saved widgets/...`, but the chat-facing result said `Proposed, not saved`. This contradictory status caused the assistant to claim the chart was unsaved, attempt a separate save, and direct the person to a Save button they could not find.
  > Make the widget tool’s chat-facing result and visible UI reflect the same persisted state. If the widget is saved by the tool, return `saved` with its name and do not describe it as awaiting the person’s Save action. If it is only a proposal, do not report an inner save as complete; clearly show the person the actual Save control and return an unsaved status. Never return both statuses for one widget.
- `context:input/guide` (0.98): The guide explains that forms can be reused, but does not distinguish saving a form for later from displaying it now. That ambiguity led to reopening a form when the person only wanted it handy, duplicating the saved form, and ending with required fields unfilled.
  > `input/get_input` displays a form now and asks the person to fill it; it is not a way to pin or merely list a form. If the person asks to keep a form handy for later, search for the matching saved form. If it exists, tell the person its name and that it can be run again; do not call `input/get_input` unless they want to fill it now. When making a form, reuse a saved form that asks for the same fields instead of creating a duplicate. After displaying a form for completion, end the turn and wait for the answers; do not say it was completed or submitted unless the returned result confirms that.

### Rep 2: weak 5/10

The assistant created a reading log and correctly summarized the three entries against Emma’s goal, while being candid that it couldn’t save them. But it never managed to save the entries or create the requested progress view, and its promise to keep a running list here doesn’t provide a reliable persistent log.

- ✓ Created the reading-log table and a form for future entries.
- ✓ Calculated the total, average, and goal comparison accurately.
- ✓ Clearly disclosed that the entries were not saved and the progress view was not created.
- ✗ Repeatedly sent invalid arguments to the database tool, leaving all three entries unsaved.
- ✗ Could not create the requested chart or other progress view.
- ✗ Promised to keep a running list in chat without establishing a dependable way to persist future entries.
- ✗ Assumed the entries were from 2026 without confirming the year.

Cause **tool-error**, layer **instructions**. Fix: Use the database write function with correctly structured arguments, then create and verify the requested progress widget before promising persistent tracking.

**Checks failed:** no-run-errors (21 of 48 tool calls failed, had invalid input or got an error or refusal back: database/create_table (invalid-input), widgets/make_widget (invalid-input), widgets/make_widget (failed), propose (tool-error), database/run_query (invalid-input), database/at_instance (invalid-input))

6 turns · 48 runs · 35 model calls · hub $0.0723 · person $0.0016 · 147s · ended: satisfied (I have a simple running list with Emma’s minutes compared against her 20-minute goal, and a format to send future entries.)

**Diagnosis:** The earliest setup failure was the difficult database row-type shape at step 4; an example helped the model recover, but the prompt never explained the reusable form workflow or that nightly activity cannot happen automatically, so it created no form (steps 9 and 17). The widget helper saw an empty source with only a table visual at step 12, and its nested draft schema and list-value errors led to invalid retries at steps 15–16 instead of postponing the chart until data existed. Most importantly, `database/run_query` described `args` as an object but its tool schema did not declare an object shape; after the result explicitly said “Send the object itself,” the model repeatedly sent lists, strings, or omitted arguments (steps 21–32), leaving all entries unsaved. It then implied persistence at steps 34–35 despite that history, and stated 2026 as fact without confirming the year.

- `system-prompt` (0.94): The prompt lists systems but does not explain reusable forms, how to use them for repeated data entry, the difference between a form and a plain question, or that the app cannot schedule or collect entries later. It also does not forbid promises of persistence without a successful save.
  > A tool (also called an “fn” here) is an action you can call. Some tools create reusable items: a database table stores rows; a saved database query reads or writes those rows; an input form asks several structured questions and can be shown again; a widget is a saved view of a table-returning tool. Use `input/get_input` when the person needs to provide several fields repeatedly; use `hub/ask_user` for a plain question that does not need a reusable form. After showing a form, end your turn and wait for the person's answers in the next message. The app does not run tasks on a schedule, send reminders, or collect information later by itself. Tell the person when they must return and submit an entry. Say that data or a view is saved only after a tool result confirms it; otherwise say exactly …
- `tool-description:database/run_query` (0.96): The schema for `args` has no declared object type, and the description's example was not enough to prevent repeated list, string, and missing-argument calls.
  > Run a saved database query with its arguments. For a query that writes, the person must approve the write. `args` must be a JSON object whose keys are the query's parameter names—not a list and not a string containing JSON. Example: for `reading_log_create(reading_date: date, minutes: num)`, call with `args: {"reading_date":"2026-11-18","minutes":25}`. Include every required parameter. If validation rejects the call, follow the exact error; do not repeat the same invalid shape.
- `tool-description:database/create_table` (0.91): The row-type schema is large and nested; the description says “row type” but gives no compact example in the tool definition.
  > Create a table from a gin row type. Use `{"name":"obj","props":{...}}`; each column is a property definition with a nested `type`. Example: `{"name":"obj","props":{"reading_date":{"type":{"name":"date"}},"minutes":{"type":{"name":"num","options":{"whole":true}}}}}`. Do not set the type name to the table name or add `extends` to this `obj` form. The person must approve the schema change.
- `fn-instructions:widgets/make_widget` (0.85): The helper was asked for a chart while its empty source exposed only a table visual. Its nested draft schema and list-value validation error supplied no working example for a sort value, and the helper stopped without a proposal.
  > If the source has no rows and the requested chart visual is not listed, do not conclude that a chart can never be made. When the user has supplied historical data, arrange for it to be recorded first, then inspect the source again and propose the best visual the populated source supports. If no chart visual is available, propose the closest supported table and clearly disclose that it is not a chart. In a draft, `show` must be exactly `control`, `pinned`, or `hidden`; never use `fixed`. If an optional sort control's value fails validation and no valid encoding is shown, omit that control rather than guessing or retrying the same invalid value. Provide one complete valid draft, including required action fields such as `bind`, when proposing an action.

1 turns · 39 runs · 24 model calls · hub $0.0757 · person $0.0004 · 72s · ended: error (the person couldn't fill "Nightly Reading Log": Fill in How many minutes did she read?.)

**Diagnosis:** At step 3 the model noticed that the goal was unknown but did not use the available question tool to ask for it or for recent entries, so the log and view were created without the information needed to show meaningful progress. The schema at steps 6–7 was hard to use without a compact example, and the widget argument schema at step 12 did not explain that `args` must be an object. The form agent knowingly described a date as a default at step 15 even though its field format could not set one, and the form interaction failed at step 18. The widget source exposed only a table for the empty result at step 20; the sort validator then rejected a value matching its advertised schema at step 21. Finally, contradictory save status from the widget run led to the wrong save instruction at step 24, which also included an unsupported reminder claim.

- `system-prompt` (0.90): The prompt says “Use tools when they help” but does not tell the model to ask for missing facts needed to set up a useful tracker, or to distinguish an actual field default from text describing a suggested date. It also lacks a clear rule against unsupported claims.
  > When a tracking or progress request depends on facts the person has not supplied—such as a target, recent entries, or which person to track—ask a concise follow-up with `hub/ask_user` before creating the tracker. Do not guess or silently omit those facts if they affect the requested result. A form is a set of questions; do not say a field is prefilled or has a default unless the form tool actually sets that value. In your final answer, state only actions and capabilities supported by tool results or this prompt. If a detail was not checked, say so rather than presenting it as fact.
- `tool-description:database/create_table` (0.94): The row-type description uses app terminology and the nested schema is large; the required per-column `type` wrapper is easy to miss.
  > The `type` value must be an inline object type. Put each column under `props`, and give each column a `type` field. Example: `{"name":"obj","props":{"id":{"type":{"name":"num","options":{"whole":true}}},"reading_date":{"type":{"name":"date"}},"minutes":{"type":{"name":"num","options":{"whole":true}}}}}`. Do not put a column's type or documentation directly beside the column name; wrap the type as shown.
- `tool-description:widgets/make_widget` (0.97): The `args` parameter has no useful shape description, although the tool rejects arrays and requires an object.
  > Use `args` as a JSON object whose keys are source argument names and whose values are their values; never pass an array of key/value records. Example: `{"args":{"limit":100}}`. Omit `args` if the source has no arguments you need to set.
- `hub-behaviour` (0.99): The person could not enter and submit a value for the required “How many minutes did she read?” form field.
  > Fix the chat form renderer and submission path so a required numeric field accepts a user-entered number and includes it in the submitted answers. Add an interaction test that fills and submits a required number field such as “How many minutes did she read?” and verifies the answer is returned.
- `hub-behaviour` (0.88): For an empty result with a date column and numeric minutes column, the widget source exposed only the table visual, so the requested line chart was unavailable to the model.
  > When determining widget visuals, use the source's column types as well as sample rows. Offer a time/line visual when the source has a date or time column and a numeric measure, even if the current result has zero rows.
- `hub-behaviour` (0.96): The widget proposal validator rejected a list value that matched its advertised schema, and the outer `widgets/make_widget` result said “Proposed, not saved” even though the nested `offer` result confirmed the widget was saved.
  > Make widget proposal validation accept the documented list-value representation for source arguments. Have `widgets/make_widget` report the final persisted state after its nested save step; it must not say “Proposed, not saved” when the widget was saved.

items.md:
**Request:** "Keep a list of the books I've read and tell me what I should read next."

**Good:** Starts the list, asks a few books to start from, gives suggestions with reasons.

Mean 6.7/10 · verdicts differ · $0.157

### Rep 1: weak 6/10

The assistant eventually saved all four books and gave three relevant picks with reasons. But its first attempt used invalid table schemas, then it incorrectly said saving was unavailable, so the person had to ask again before the list was actually stored.

- ✓ Asked one useful question covering books read and reading preferences.
- ✓ Saved all four books with ratings and verified the rows were present.
- ✓ Recommended three fitting books and gave reasons, including standalone sci-fi and memoirs.
- ✗ Two invalid table-creation calls failed before the correct schema was used.
- ✗ Initially said it could not save the list even though it later created and populated a persistent table.
- ✗ The person had to repeat the request to get the list saved.

Cause **gave-up**, layer **context**. Fix: Use the available table-creation example or schema guidance after an invalid-input error, and keep trying before telling the person saving is unavailable.

**Checks failed:** no-run-errors (2 of 37 tool calls failed, had invalid input or got an error or refusal back: database/create_table (invalid-input))

2 turns · 37 runs · 28 model calls · hub $0.0724 · person $0.0005 · 95s · ended: satisfied (My book list is saved, and I have three good next picks.)

**Diagnosis:** The first table call at step 12 used the wrong nested field shape; although `database/create_table` exposed a very large schema, no concise example was included alongside it. After the first rejection, step 13 guessed another shape, and step 14 loaded a guide about a different data mechanism instead of using `hub/fn_examples`. The system prompt's instruction to stop when a call “keeps failing” and the tool error's “fix it and try again” did not give a clear recovery path. At step 15 the assistant turned two malformed attempts into the unsupported conclusion that persistent saving was unavailable, and also named *Born a Crime* without a supporting search result. The person had to repeat the request; the example at step 17 enabled the correct table creation and the later save and verification succeeded.

- `system-prompt` (0.94): The prompt says to stop when “the same call keeps failing” but does not distinguish a malformed argument from an unavailable capability or explain how to recover. It also does not explain that `data_sets` lists the hub's predefined record types, not SQL database tables, or that the database can create a persistent table and reusable functions for adding and listing rows.
  > A `fn` is a tool. The `database` system stores persistent rows in SQL tables. `hub/data_sets` lists the hub's predefined record types; an empty result there does not mean SQL tables cannot be created. When a person asks to keep a new list or other structured collection, search for and use the database table-creation tool if available. After creating a table, use the database tools to generate and run functions for adding and listing its rows. A rejected call with an invalid-input or schema error is not proof that the capability is unavailable: read the error, consult `hub/fn_examples` for that function or load the relevant database guide, then retry with the documented shape. Stop only when the corrected call is refused, the capability is genuinely unavailable, or a corrected attempt stil…
- `tool-description:database/create_table` (0.96): The tool exposed a very large nested type schema. Its description said an object type has `props`, but did not show that every property definition must wrap its type in a `type` field; the model's first two calls were rejected.
  > Create a persistent SQL table. The `type` argument is an inline object type: use `{"name":"obj","props":{...}}`. Each column definition must wrap its column type in `type`; do not put the type directly in the column definition. Example: `{"table":"books_read","type":{"name":"obj","props":{"id":{"type":{"name":"text"}},"title":{"type":{"name":"text"}},"year_read":{"type":{"name":"num","options":{"whole":true}}}}}}`. If a call is rejected, consult `hub/fn_examples` for this function and use a documented shape instead of guessing. The table change waits for the person's approval.
- `system-prompt` (0.96): The response claimed saving was unavailable even though the only evidence was that two submitted schemas were rejected. It also recommended *Born a Crime* without a supporting tool result. The prompt says to use tools and say what was done, but does not explicitly require factual and action claims to be grounded in returned results.
  > Ground claims about actions and facts in tool results. Say a list is saved only after a successful write, and say you verified it only after a read result confirms it. **Request:** "When did I last change the furnace filter? I never remember this stuff."

**Good:** Admits it doesn't know yet, offers to start a home-maintenance log, asks for the date.

Mean 5.7/10 · same verdict every rep · $0.0769

### Rep 1: weak 5/10

The assistant honestly said it couldn’t find a filter-change record, calculated the next due date correctly, and was clear that Google Calendar wasn’t connected. But it didn’t ask for the date or offer to start a maintenance log, and it never recorded the date once the user provided it.

- ✓ Reported that it found no filter-change record and distinguished the tune-up invoice from a filter change.
- ✓ Calculated the filter was due around Nov 3, 2026, and gave useful recurring dates.
- ✓ Clearly explained it could not create a Google Calendar reminder and gave setup steps.
- ✗ Didn’t ask when the filter was last changed or offer to start a maintenance log.
- ✗ Didn’t save the Aug 3 change date or filter interval after the user supplied them.
- ✗ One file-search call used an invalid regular expression, though a later search succeeded.

Cause **didnt-ask**, layer **chat-prompt**. Fix: When no change record is found, ask for the last-change date and offer to log it; once provided, save the maintenance details if the available tools allow it.

**Checks failed:** no-run-errors (1 of 17 tool calls failed, had invalid input or got an error or refusal back: fs/grep (failed))

**Diagnosis:** The prompt never explained what to do when a personal-history search finds no record, or that the database can be used to create a reusable log and save later entries; it only says that database queries are kept as an fn, without explaining that a table can be created for new personal records or how to persist them. So at step 10 the assistant stopped after saying `I couldn’t find a record`, and at steps 11–14 it focused on reminders instead of recording the newly supplied date and interval. The prompt also never says that scheduled runs and proactive reminders do not exist, leaving the step 14 limitation claim without explicit support at that point. Separately, step 4 used a regex flag the grep tool does not accept, and the search at step 2 surfaced an unrelated reading log and developer material.

- `system-prompt` (0.91): The prompt says to use tools and lists the database and input systems, but does not explain how to handle missing personal history, create a reusable log, save details the person provides, or distinguish forms from plain questions. It also omits the lack of scheduled runs and notifications.

  > For searches phrased as everyday questions about a person's household or personal records, rank matching user data and task-relevant functions ahead of developer and system-authoring documentation. Do not return unrelated functions such as a reading log as leading results merely because the request contains words like “log” or “record.”

### Rep 2: weak 6/10

The assistant was honest that it had no record, later saved the date and interval in memory, and clearly explained that it could not schedule alerts or add a calendar event. But its first reply didn’t offer to start a maintenance log or ask for the date as the Good line calls for; the user had to volunteer that information.

- ✓ Was clear that no furnace-filter record was available.
- ✓ Saved the user’s update in memory and calculated the due date.
- ✓ Did not claim to schedule or add anything; gave useful Google Calendar steps.
- ✗ Didn’t proactively ask for the last-change date or offer to start a home-maintenance log.
- ✗ Used many searches before giving the simple answer.

Cause **didnt-ask**, layer **chat-prompt**. Fix: When no record exists, say so, offer to start a maintenance log, and ask when the filter was last changed.

5 turns · 22 runs · 26 model calls · hub $0.0359 · person $0.0015 · 94s · ended: satisfied (I got the steps to set it up, and the assistant was clear it can’t add the event directly.)

**Diagnosis:** At step 1, the system prompt said only “Use tools when they help” and “Find fns and context with hub/fns_search”; it did not explain a quick no-record workflow or how to offer a reusable log. The systems list said database queries are kept “as a fn for next time” and input can “keep good forms,” but it did not explain that a database table can hold a new maintenance log, that `input/get_input` can create a reusable form, or how either differs from a plain question. At steps 2–3 and 13–15, search mixed everyday tools with developer material, returning items such as “fs/authoring.data,” a reading-log query, and “fs/authoring.folder”; that encouraged unnecessary exploration. The prompt also never said that nothing runs later and that memory is only a saved note, not a notification, so the assistant had no explicit capability boundary or rule to stop searching after establishing that limitation. It eventually saved accurate notes, correctly checked for a connected calendar service, and was honest about not scheduling anything, but it missed the initial opportunity to ask for the date and offer a maintenance log.

- `system-prompt` (0.91): The prompt asks the model to search for tools but does not explain the app’s terms or guide it from “no existing record” to asking for missing information and offering ongoing tracking. The model was not told how reusable logs and forms work.
  > In this app, a **tool** is also called a **fn**; a **system** is a connected program that provides tools and data; and **context** is guidance or saved information loaded into the chat. You may not have every tool yet: search for a relevant tool, then load it before using it. Search for the user’s existing records efficiently; do not keep searching unrelated documentation after a relevant check shows no record.

When did you last change it? I can help start a home-maintenance log so you can record future changes.”

  > For searches made in ordinary user chats, rank available, user-facing operational tools and user data ahead of developer documentation, authoring guides, and implementation examples. Keep developer material searchable when explicitly requested, but do not let it dominate results for everyday tasks such as finding a household record or setting a reminder.
- `system-prompt` (0.96): The prompt does not state the scheduling limit or distinguish saving a memory from creating an alert. The model searched repeatedly for reminders, including at step 18 after it had already said it could not schedule them.
  > Nothing in this app runs automatically later: tools cannot schedule future or repeating tasks or send proactive reminders. A saved **memory** is only a note that may be available in a later chat; it does not trigger an alert. If asked to schedule a reminder, say this clearly and offer a practical alternative, such as instructions for setting one in a calendar. You may check the connected API services for a calendar integration; if no suitable service is listed, do not try to create an API connection or imply that an event was added. **Diagnosis:** At steps 4–5, the database search surfaced `database/main.reading_log_create` but not the available table-creation path, and the prompt did not explain that `database/create_table` can propose a new table subject to approval; the agent then made the unsupported claim that it had no way to add one.
